steps: Here Maya asks Claude, in an ordinary chat, for a ten step client onboarding procedure.
Claude answers right there in the chat. But thirty turns later, the procedure is buried in scrollback, and Maya cannot even remember which chat it was in.
Then a colleague shows her Artifacts. Since the team will reuse this procedure, Maya asks again, this time as an Artifact.
Claude judges the content substantial and reusable, so it renders it in the side panel, apart from the chat, as version one, saved.
Two days later, Maya opens the same Artifact and asks Claude to add a step. It is edited in place, becoming version two.
Next, instead of pasting it into an email, she shares the stable link with her manager, who can view, comment or edit.
Finally, the manager opens the link and sees the latest version, version two, with no scrollback hunt. Reusable work deserves a permanent home.
